mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and depressing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5% mean) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction of more than 10% month-over-month indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST m/m change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1% mean) during episodes where GDPC1 YoY < -2% and HOUST m/m < -10%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market that amplifies wage inflation, eroding corporate profit margins and ultimately producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5% mean) during periods of three consecutive months with UNRATE < 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings visibility and increases risk premia, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO m/m change < -0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5% mean) during four consecutive months of INDPRO m/m < -0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a decline in consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) below 2% over two months signals a disinflationary tightening, which increases real interest rates and depresses growth-sensitive equities, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases AND CPIAUCSL < 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1% mean) during periods of simultaneous FEDFUNDS increases and CPIAUCSL < 2% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth > 0.4%) combined with a monthly rise in retail sales (RSAFS growth > 0.3%) signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS m/m growth > 0.4% AND RSAFS m/m growth > 0.3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5% mean) during periods of PAYEMS m/m > 0.4% and RSAFS m/m > 0.3%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.0% for five consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation risk, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate preemptive Fed tightening and higher growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.7% mean) during five consecutive months of UNRATE < 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth (GDPC1) above 4% for three consecutive quarters signals a robust demand environment, which supports earnings momentum and reduces recession risk, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 q/q growth > 4% for 3 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1.0% mean) during three consecutive quarters of GDPC1 q/q > 4%.
